subject: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification - context window & latency impact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@finco.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification - context window & latency impact

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the FinCo team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end so we can align on SLOs and test plan.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workload: real-time account summarization for advisor dashboards (single-turn generation).
- Expected peak concurrency: 120 concurrent requests during market hours; baseline 40 rps.
- Typical payloads: user history + 2-3 documents ~ avg 6k tokens in, target output ~ 300-600 tokens.
- Latency target: 95th pct <= 350ms token-streaming enabled; prefer streaming for UX.
- Hard constraint: end-to-end 95th pct under 700ms for critical flows.

Open questions we noted:
1) Confirm max context window requirement (we discussed up to 32k but need distribution of input sizes).
2) Clarify whether any workloads require synchronous multi-turn back-and-forth within a single request.
3) Acceptable tradeoffs for quantization/throughput vs final-quality (any strict hallucination constraints?).

Next steps (proposed):
- John / Amy: share a sampled payload distribution (histogram or 200 sample requests) and any SLAs in writing (we can use the attached SLO_requirements.xlsx template).
- Rishi: draft test plan for concurrency and streaming profiling (we'll attach expected load scripts).
- Marissa: schedule a 60-minute perf sync next week to run through test results and pin latency SLOs.

Attachments: SLO_requirements.xlsx (template), latency-test-results.pdf (example from similar customer).

If this all looks right, I'll book the perf sync for next Tue/Wed — please reply with preferred times.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: John Lee <john.lee@finco.com>

Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification - context window & latency impact

Thanks, Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Context window: our max occasionally hits ~28k tokens (aggregated long notes + attachments). The distribution is skewed: ~70% under 8k, 20% between 8k-20k, 10% over 20k up to 28k. We'll export a 200-sample set today.
- Latency: target for advisor dashboard flows is 95th <= 400ms (streaming preferred). For nightly bulk summarization batch jobs there is no strict latency SLO.
- Concurrency: 120 concurrent during peak is accurate; we can throttle non-critical requests to off-peak.
- Streaming: must receive partial tokens within 150ms for first chunk otherwise UX jitter is unacceptable.

We'll upload the sample payloads to the Drive link you shared by EOD. One more ask: do you have a recommended batching/caching config for our workload?

Regards,
John
John Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | FinCo
john.lee@finco.com

2) We recommend starting with a 95th <= 400ms pilot for the advisor flow; if tests show regression we can iterate on model variant (quantized vs fp16) and routing.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification - context window & latency impact

John / team — quick engineering notes ahead of the perf sync.

- Streaming first-chunk goal: we can reliably push first partial tokens within 100-150ms for inputs <= 12k tokens using our default streaming path and continuous batching. For larger inputs we use progressive KV-prefetch to prioritize early tokens; expectation is first-chunk within 150-250ms depending on model variant and network hop.
- Concurrency & throughput: to meet 120 concurrent with 95th <= 400ms we recommend starting with the following config in the pilot: 8 reserved vGPU slots (dedicated), max batch size 16, prefetch window 4k tokens, and async KV-loading enabled. We'll include an autoscale headroom of +30% for traffic spikes.
- Tokenization/encoding notes: please ensure the sample payloads include raw UTF text and any base64 attachments separated; token counts need to be accurate (we'll run a tokenizer pass).
- Test plan attachments: I've attached a preliminary load script and latency-test-results.pdf from an internal benchmark to show expected curves vs context window.

We'll validate on Tue and iterate on quantization profile if we see tail latency issues. Marissa — I'll join the perf sync and bring a short runbook for measuring 95/99 pct and streaming chunk timings.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: redwood-prefetch-config.json, latency-test-results.pdf
